title: Evaluation of Differences in Individual Treatment Response in Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders: A Meta-analysis

cost.compute_notes: OSF deposit: response.csv 30,538 B, data_dictionary 2,149 B, response_do.R 20,150 B, response_func.R 14,792 B. Abstract from Europe PMC. Six analysis scripts w01-w06. Longest is w01 (46 s: 800 simulated corpora for the lambda anchors plus two 4000-draw bootstraps); w05 49 s; w06 19 s. Total simulation wall clock about 2 min.

claims.statement: The variability of outcome was slightly lower in the antipsychotic arms than in placebo arms: VR = 0.97 (95% CI 0.95-0.99, P = .01) across 52 RCTs and 15,360 patients, so there is no evidence that antipsychotics increase outcome variance and hence no personal element of response.
claims.scope: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs of licensed antipsychotics in schizophrenia spectrum disorders to 2016; PANSS pre-post difference scores.

our_assessment.why: The measurement reproduces exactly from the deposited data -- k, both patient totals and the pooled VR to three decimals, under their own pooling and under two alternatives. Accepted as a measurement. NOT accepted as the inference: VR significantly BELOW 1 is not 'no increase', it is incompatible with their own null model (see c3), and the deviation is the same size as a bias their design carries (c4).

quantities.name: baseline_variability_ratio_negative_control
quantities.source: maria 2026, w02 -- the same statistic on BASELINE SDs, p = 0.173; randomisation behaves, so the endpoint deficit is not an allocation or extraction artifact

our_assessment.why: Accepted as a measurement of D, with three robustness checks and a passing negative control. The INFERENCE that it refutes rho = 0 is NOT accepted -- see c4. What survives without qualification is the weaker and still-unstated point: every paper in this area reads VR near or below 1 as 'no heterogeneity', and under their own decomposition a VR below 1 cannot be produced by any non-negative sigma_TE at rho = 0. The direction of the deviation carries information they do not use.

claims.statement: MARIA 2026, NEW: the boundedness of the outcome scale is a fifth axis of non-identification. PANSS cannot fall below 30, the treated arm improves more and therefore meets that bound more often, and truncation removes variance from the treated arm specifically. A simulated world with sigma_TE = 0 EXACTLY reproduces between 23% and 112% of the observed negative D, depending on the baseline mean -- which the deposit does not record.
claims.scope: Simulation using each trial's own baseline SD from the deposit and the same change SD in both arms. Baseline mean swept from 75 to 100 because it is absent from the data.

our_assessment.why: The claim has no truth value until someone supplies the baseline mean, which is exactly the sense 'not-identifiable' is for. At a baseline of 80 the floor is the whole effect; at 95 it is a third. Both are inside the plausible range for acute schizophrenia trials and the deposit records sd0 but not mu0. What IS established without that field: the floor-induced bias is of the same order as every effect ever reported in this literature (1-3%), it always runs in the same direction at these headrooms, no paper accounts for it, and the correct null for VR is therefore a few per cent below 1 rather than 1.

claims.statement: MARIA 2026: the within-corpus test that would settle whether the floor mechanism is real has NO RESOLVING POWER on the available data, and the correction in c4 therefore remains model-based.
claims.scope: 68 HAMD17 trials with a reported baseline mean (the antipsychotic deposit cannot support the test at all). Regression of lnVR on the predicted per-trial floor bias, with both anchors simulated.

quantities.name: floor_test_predicted_bias_span
quantities.source: maria 2026, w06 -- against a per-trial lnVR sampling SD of 0.104; the signal is at the level of one trial's noise

our_assessment.why: Recorded as a failure with the same care as a finding, because the first version of this test produced a publishable-looking artifact. The regressor z = (baseline - mean change)/SD contains the same arm SDs as lnVR = log(s1/s2), so regressor and outcome are coupled by construction. Holding the regressor fixed across simulated replicates broke that coupling in the null ONLY, and reported 'observed -1.197 against a null of +0.010, p < 0.001, inconsistent with both'. Recomputing the regressor inside each replicate moves the no-floor null to -2.189: the entire -1.2 was coupling. With the null right, the two anchors are separated by less than their own noise, so the tool now refuses to print the ratio and says why.

our_assessment.why: Worth recording positively and precisely, because the cost difference is measurable and because the failure that remains is instructive: a complete, well-licensed, executable deposit whose data dictionary lists sd0tx and sd0ct but no baseline MEAN. Completeness is judged against the question, not against a checklist. Every artifact-badging scheme in existence would pass this deposit, and the field it omits is the one that decides whether its headline survives.

relations.why: Same design, same statistic, same conclusion in a different disease: the variability ratio is at or below 1 and is read as absence of individual response.

Ploderl & Hengartner state that they followed 'the procedure suggested by Winkelbeiner et al.' and cite this OSF node. The methodological lineage is explicit, which is why a bias in the procedure propagates to both.
relations.asymmetric_note: The direction is Ploderl copying Winkelbeiner, so a defect here is inherited there and not vice versa.

relations.why: McCutcheon et al. argue a VR near 1 is compatible with large sigma_TE once rho is negative. This record adds that on the antipsychotic corpus VR is significantly BELOW 1, which under their own decomposition cannot be produced by any non-negative sigma_TE at rho = 0 -- so the direction of the deviation, not just its size, is informative. It also supplies a mechanism they do not consider that produces the same sign with no rho at all.

Both treat an outcome bounded below as though it were unbounded, so both compare VR to a null of exactly 1 when the no-heterogeneity null on their scales is a few per cent below it. Neither cites the other on this because neither states it.

Senn's four components are a variance decomposition of an unbounded quantity. On a bounded scale the decomposition itself acquires a bias term that is not any of A, B, C or D, and whose size here is comparable to the effects being argued about.

open_questions: The floor correction has a bootstrap interval on only one of its two inputs. Model uncertainty -- truncated normal versus whatever the real bounded response distribution is -- is not represented at all.
Baseline PANSS means for these 52 trials would settle the sweep in c4 outright. They are in the papers; the deposit dropped them.

The two remaining psychiatric variability meta-analyses (PTSD psychotherapy, depression psychotherapy) both use bounded scales and both report VR near 1. The same correction applies and has never been made.

Is there a bounded-outcome literature outside psychiatry where this bias has been named? The mechanism is generic to any capped improvement measure, and it would be surprising if nobody has written it down -- but nothing in the three psychiatric papers cites such a source.
